name: tag_delete

path.udtDefinitionNamespace: under an explicit _types_ allowlist entry, or under * when allowlistsWildcardIncludeUdtTypes is true
path.cascade: a Folder target takes everything beneath it in one system.tag.deleteTags call, so the token the caller reasons about is the Folder's own configuration

nativeOutcome: one system.tag.deleteTags call per item, with the target as a one-element path list; its single QualityCode is that item's outcome, and Observed state never decides success

preconditionToken.comparedRead: system.tag.exists(path) and then system.tag.getConfiguration(path, false, false) for every item, before any item executes
preconditionToken.raceWindow: D30 2: the compare and the change are two steps, so a competing writer can change or remove a target between the Preflight read and system.tag.deleteTags. The handler narrows what it can (every fingerprint is read before any dispatch, and a target the Preflight read found missing is refused with not_found) and claims no atomicity. A target rewritten inside the window is deleted with content the caller never saw, which is the deletion the token was there to guard, so a caller that needs a narrower window re-reads with tag_get_config and retries the whole batch.

preflight: input, reserved provider and Target allowlist for every item before any item executes, with no rollback

runtimeTargetPolicy.allowlistMatch: provider-qualified config path prefix at segment boundaries; explicit * allows every provider; it includes UDT Definitions only when allowlistsWildcardIncludeUdtTypes is true
runtimeTargetPolicy.reservedProviderRefusal: permission_denied before Preflight, whatever the allowlist says, including an explicit *: a delete inside the policy provider would remove the document every Runtime Mutation reads (owner ruling 1)

targetPath.form: <provider>Tag, <provider>Folder or <provider>Folder/Tag, and <provider>_types_/... for a UDT definition
targetPath.noWildcard: a config target is one exact path: a *, ? or : anywhere in it is invalid_argument
targetPath.leaf: the target's last segment names the node the call removes, and one path-list entry is one target: the handler never expands a Folder into its children

udtDefinitionTargets: A UDT Definition target whose first post-provider segment is _types_ is allowed by a matching explicit _types_ allowlist entry, or by * when allowlistsWildcardIncludeUdtTypes is true. When the property is absent or false, * does not cover UDT Definitions. A folder named _types_ deeper in the path remains an ordinary target.
missingTargetFails: not_found (details.items[].reason = targetMissing): a target the Preflight existence check does not find refuses the whole batch before anything is dispatched, so a delete never creates a node it was asked to remove
collisionPolicyWhy: system.tag.deleteTags takes no collision policy: it removes exactly the provider-qualified paths it is given and writes nothing at another path, so there is no destination that could collide and no D30 4 knob for the handler to fix
ambiguousOutcomeScope: an item whose own dispatch raised is outcome_unknown and ends the batch (later items are not_executed); an item whose dispatch answered an unattributable QualityCode is outcome_unknown and the batch continues. Nothing is replayed

existenceCheck.call: system.tag.exists(path) for every item, before that item's fingerprint is read and before any item executes
existenceCheck.why: a Gateway answers system.tag.getConfiguration for a path that is not there with a synthesized default node, so the configuration read alone cannot tell the caller whether the target exists; the ticket #10 live run recorded the same synthesized node on 8.3.8 and 8.3.9
existenceCheck.missing: not_found (details.items[].reason = targetMissing), and nothing is dispatched
existenceCheck.unanswered: upstream_error (reasons existenceCheckFailed / existenceCheckIndeterminate): a Gateway that raises or answers something that is not a boolean is never read as present
existenceCheck.observedReadBacks: the provider export is the independent absence check the harness uses

inputBounds.hardItemsPolicyRule: a deployment may raise the 20-target default through the Runtime Target Policy and never above the 100-target hard ceiling

observedState: the deleted target's own absence, read back per item with `system.tag.exists(path)` and reported as `absent: true`; a target the Gateway still answers as present is an explicit `upstream_error` observed error, never a silent omission. It is Observed state and never decides success, and a delete leaves no fingerprint behind: the caller's next tag_get_config of that path is a not_found
deniedMutationAudit: after a usable Policy is read, a refused Target and a refused Precondition each produce one `decision` row and no dispatch; `off` records nothing, and `required` refuses the call when the denial row cannot be written
outcomePreservation: a dispatched batch reports its per-item Native outcomes whatever the Observed-state read and the serializer do; an Observed state that cannot be returned turns into an explicit observed error on every reported path, and the result is re-rendered without the Observed state rather than replacing the outcomes
